title: Construction of Model Lipid Membranes Incorporating G-protein Coupled Receptors (GPCRs)
protocol: Label NHS-rhodamine in 100 µL DMSO with 5 µL 1 M sodium bicarbonate solution.
Add 3.66 µL of labeled NHS-rhodamine solution to 50 µL of 5-HT1AR solution and mix gently.
Protect the mixture from light and incubate at room temperature on a rotator for 1 hour.
Wash a 7 k MWCO spin column three times with 200 µL of 1x PBS for 1.5 min each time at 1.5 RCF.
Add the labeled protein to the spin column and balance any remaining solution in another tube.
Spin down the labeled protein once for 5 min at 1.5 RCF.
Measure UV-vis spectrum using a nanodrop spectrophotometer at 280 nm and 554 nm.
Calculate labeling efficiency according to the manufacturer's manual.
Store the labeled protein covered at 5 °C until further use.
Clean coverslips by placing them in methanol.
Sonicate coverslips for 30 min at 40 °C.
Dry excess methanol on coverslips with a gentle stream of air.
Place dried coverslips in a 40 °C oven for 15 min.
Begin plasma cleaning process.
Place coverslips into the plasma cleaner and close off the air intake valve to evacuate all air inside the chamber.
Clean coverslips for 5 min using high RF power setting with near complete vacuum.
Adjust opening of the vacuum chamber to ensure a steady, bright pink plasma color.
Shut off RF power once cleaning is completed.
Release the vacuum in the chamber.
Combine 6 mg of ultra-low melting temperature agarose with 300 µL of ultrapure water (i.e., 2% (w/v) agarose).
Vortex the 2% agarose solution briefly before placing it on a 90 °C heat block for 10 min.
Transfer the 2% agarose solution to a 45 °C heat block and keep it in the molten form until further use.
Combine 9 mg of ultra-low temperature agarose with 300 µL of ultrapure water (i.e., 3% (w/v) agarose).
Vortex the 3% agarose solution briefly before placing it on a 90 °C heat block for 10 min.
Transfer the 3% agarose solution to a 45 °C heat block and keep it in the molten form until further use.
Mix 21 µL of 3% agarose with the 7 µL of 5-HT1AR membrane fragments.
Pipette up and down slowly many times to ensure adequate mixing.
Incubate the mixture at 45 °C for 1 min.
Make a thin film on freshly plasma-cleaned coverslips using 20 µL of 2% agarose.
Quickly drop another coverslip on top of the agarose droplet and gently slide the coverslips apart to make a thin film on both coverslips.
Pipette the protein/agarose mixture up and down one more time, and then deposit 20 µL of the 2% agarose on a plasma-cleaned coverslip.
Allow the agarose to gel protected from light for 30 min at room temperature.
Deposit 10 µL of a lipid mixture containing 2 mg/mL POPC with 0.4 Mol% ATTO-488-DPPE in chloroform dropwise on top of the agarose layer.
Spread one droplet at a time using a gas chromatography needle and a gentle air stream to form a relatively uniform layer of lipids.
Place an O-ring on top of the coverslip.
Position the top component of the chamber onto the O-ring.
Screw together the chamber components using the key provided by the manufacturer to seal the chamber.
Ensure the chamber is sealed tightly enough to prevent leakage when swelling solution is added.
Hydrate the system by gently pipetting 450 μL of 200 mM sucrose in 1x PBS.
Gently tap the chambers to ensure adequate buffer coverage of the hydrogel-lipid layers.
Place the chambers at 45 °C and cover with a coverslip to prevent evaporation.
Allow the sample to swell, protected from debris and light for 1 h.
Add 100 μL of 1 mg/mL BSA in ultrapure water into each well of a 96-well plate.
Incubate at room temperature for 1 h.
Wash three times with ultra-pure water.
Wash once with 200 mM sucrose in 1x PBS.
Add 200 mM glucose in 1x PBS until the addition of the GUV sample solution.
Gently shake and tap the chamber to dislodge any GUVs that may remain attached to the hydrogel surface.
Pipette up the GUV-sucrose solution.
Move the suspension into a microcentrifuge tube containing 700 μL of 200 mM glucose in 1x PBS.
Allow the vesicles to settle for an additional hour.
Transfer 300 μL of settled vesicles from the bottom of the centrifuge tube into a BSA-treated 96-well plate.
Avoid transferring debris at the very bottom of the microcentrifuge tube.
Examine the samples under a confocal microscope.
Shine a 488 nm laser on the sample to visualize the membrane labeled with ATTO-488-DPPE.
Shine a 561 nm laser on the sample to visualize the protein labeled with NHS-Rhodamine.
